description: A dataset of floating debris accumulation at bridges after July 2021 flood in Germany and Belgium is a data set described in a peer-reviewed Scientific Data article written by Sébastien Erpicum et al. This paper presents a dataset documenting 71 floating debris accumulations at bridges following an extreme hydrological event that hit Belgium and Germany in July 2021. Data were collected from various sources including public authorities’ documents, public online databases, post event pictures and field visits. The dataset covers bridges geometry, flood conditions and debris accumulation. Coverage: several countries (DE, BE); published in 2024. Formats: CSV. The data are held in RWTH Aachen University and reached through its DOI listed on this page; the paper's Data Records section names it. Size stated by the repository: pages 1-10. Access is free of charge and open according to the article. The licence of the data is not stated in the sources read (the paper itself is open access). Caveats: written from the Scientific Data article metadata (title, abstract, Data Records section) read on 2026-10-01; the data themselves were not opened or downloaded, so their contents, quality and current availability were not checked. It can support transport-network, traffic and mobility studies. Related records: none catalogued yet.
